A serene coastal village in central Vietnam's coastal region, known as a "làng chài," is shown with traditional fishing boats called "thúng," crafted from woven bamboo and rattan, resting on a golden sandy beach. This makes them lightweight, easy to maneuver, and able to reach fishing spots inaccessible to other boats. These boats are also used in local schools to teach children about traditional crafts and sustainable fishing practices. In contrast to modern fishing vessels, which often rely on motor power and are less adaptable to varied water conditions, "thúng" boats showcase the ingenuity and resourcefulness of the local fishing community. The use of natural materials and traditional techniques not only supports sustainable fishing practices but also preserves the cultural identity of the region, making these boats a vital part of Vietnamese heritage. Moreover, "thúng" boats are often featured in cultural festivals and traditions, reinforcing their importance beyond just fishing. They symbolize the community’s deep connection to the land and sea and are celebrated in local ceremonies and educational programs.
